title: Türkiye Museum Fees 2027: What Changes on 1 April and How to Budget
excerpt: New euro entry fees for foreign visitors at Ephesus, Pamukkale, Galata Tower, Cappadocia and other state sites are scheduled to start on 1 April 2027, according to ministry schedules reported in September 2026. Here is what is reported, what is still open and how to budget a trip that spans the change.

body.text: Entry to Türkiye’s state museums and archaeological sites is getting more expensive for foreign visitors in 2027 — but not on 1 January, as some early summaries assumed. The fee schedules sent out by the Culture and Tourism Ministry’s revolving-fund directorate (DÖSİMM) in September 2026, as reposted by Turkish trade sites, carry an effective date of 1 April 2027. If your trip falls in the first quarter, you pay the tariff currently published; if it runs across the start of April, part of your trip is priced on each side. This guide sets out the confirmed figures, the points that remain open, and a simple way to budget.
What is confirmed, and from when

The ministry letter, reposted in full by [Alomaliye](https://www.alomaliye.com/2026/09/08/2027-yili-muze-ve-orenyeri-giris-ucretleri-aciklandi/), revises the tariff tables attached to the ministry’s museum entry directive for 2027, based on board decisions of 27 August and 4 September 2026. The attached [MuseumPass schedule](https://www.alomaliye.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2027-muze-orenyeri-yabanci.pdf) and [combined-ticket schedule](https://www.alomaliye.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2027-muze-orenyeri-kombine.pdf) both state that the new prices apply from 1 April 2027. [FTNnews](https://ftnnews.com/travel-news/news-from-turkey/turkiye-museum-fees-2027/) reports the same date and adds that the 2026 tariff stays in force until then. Turkish trade titles such as [Turizm Güncel](https://www.turizmguncel.com/haber/muze-ve-oren-yerlerine-giris-ucretlerine-zam-2027-tarifesi-belli-oldu) published the same site prices but say only “in 2027”, which is where the January assumption came from.

One caveat: the original letter does not appear on the ministry’s own websites, and the official ticket pages on muze.gov.tr load prices dynamically, so we could not see the new amounts there. Treat the figures below as reported, announced tariffs, not as an official ministry price list, and confirm the price for your visit date on muze.gov.tr before you buy.
Main sites: foreign-visitor prices from 1 April 2027

Figures as reported by Turizm Güncel and FTNnews (which agree). In brackets, the price shown in the tariff table currently published in the [ministry directive on muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/document/bakanlik_yonergesi_tr.pdf), where we could find the same site.

items: Ephesus archaeological site (İzmir): €45 (currently €40). The muze.gov.tr [Ephesus page](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=EFS01&DistId=EFS) says the ticket includes the Ephesus Experience Museum.
Ephesus plus the Terrace Houses, combined ticket: €57 from 1 April 2027, valid 72 hours from first use.
Hierapolis–Pamukkale (Denizli): €35 (currently €30).
Galata Tower (Istanbul): €35 (currently €30).
Göreme open-air site (Cappadocia): €22 (currently €20). Zelve–Paşabağları €13 (currently €12). Kaymaklı and Derinkuyu underground cities €15 each (currently €13 each).
Istanbul Archaeology Museums (with the Museum of the Ancient Orient and Tiled Kiosk): €16 (currently €15).
Sümela Monastery (Trabzon) and Bodrum Museum of Underwater Archaeology: €22 each (Bodrum currently €20).
Mevlana Museum (Konya): free for foreign visitors, as it is in the current table.
Museum of Anatolian Civilizations (Ankara): reports disagree — Turizm Güncel lists it as free, FTNnews lists €13 (currently €12). Check before you go.

body.text: From 1 April 2027 the MuseumPass schedule lists MuseumPass Türkiye at €185 (15 days, more than 300 museums and sites) and MuseumPass İstanbul at €120 (5 days, Istanbul only). Regional cards are MuseumPass Cappadocia €75 (3 days), Aegean €105 (7 days) and Mediterranean €100 (7 days). These are separate products, listed individually on the official [MuseumPass page](https://muze.gov.tr/MuseumPass); an Istanbul card will not get you into Ephesus or Göreme. Coverage of individual sites, such as the Terrace Houses or Galata Tower, should be confirmed on each product’s detail page before you buy. If your question is only whether a pass pays off in Istanbul, use our [Istanbul pass-or-single-tickets method](/blog/istanbul-museum-pass-or-single-tickets) instead.
Budgeting a trip that spans 1 April

items: Date every paid visit. Put each site on your itinerary with its date; anything before 1 April uses the current table, anything from 1 April the new one.

Find the sites that dominate cost. On a classic route — Galata Tower, the Istanbul Archaeology Museums, Göreme, one underground city, Zelve, Pamukkale and Ephesus — single tickets add up to €181 at the 2027 prices, compared with €160 at today’s published prices. Ephesus, Pamukkale and Galata alone make up €115 of the 2027 total.

Compare with a pass only after the sum. On that example, MuseumPass Türkiye (€185) roughly matches single tickets; swap Ephesus for the €57 Ephesus–Terrace Houses ticket and singles reach €193. Whether the pass wins depends on what it actually covers and whether your visits fit its 15 days.
Don’t assume early purchase locks in the old price. We found no rule on whether a ticket bought before 1 April for a later date is honoured at the old tariff. Check the terms at checkout.

Add a currency buffer. Under the [ministry directive](https://muze.gov.tr/document/bakanlik_yonergesi_tr.pdf) euro tariffs are collected in Turkish lira at the Central Bank’s previous-day effective selling rate, so the lira amount you pay moves with the exchange rate.

Check eligibility for reductions rather than counting on them. The directive allows separate tariffs by age, profession or MüzeKart and lists free-entry exceptions in an annex; whether any applies to you depends on documents you carry. Budget at full price.

body.text: Night openings are a separate ticket

Night-museum visits are priced separately from daytime entry, and the directive states that its exemptions do not apply to them. They are also seasonal: in 2026, the muze.gov.tr homepage listed the Göreme night programme as running until 1 November. If an evening visit to Galata Tower or another site matters to your plans, check the official night-museum page for your dates rather than assuming it runs year-round.
On the day: a five-point check

items: Open the site’s page on [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/) or the official e-ticket section and check the price for your exact visit date.
Confirm which product you are buying: single site, combined ticket (Ephesus plus Terrace Houses, for example) or a MuseumPass — and which pass.
Expect to pay in lira; note the euro price so you can sanity-check the converted amount.
If you hold a pass, read its coverage for that site and check whether any part of the visit is ticketed separately.
For night openings, look for a separate night ticket and confirm the season.

body.text: Planning the route itself? Our [7-day Istanbul and Cappadocia itinerary](/blog/7-day-turkey-itinerary-istanbul-cappadocia) and [month-by-month timing guide](/blog/best-time-to-visit-turkiye-month-by-month) help you decide whether shifting a few days before or after 1 April is worth it.

seo.intent: Find out what Türkiye's main museums and archaeological sites will cost foreign visitors in 2027, from which date, and how to budget a trip that spans the change.
seo.uniqueValue: Resolves the effective date (1 April 2027, from the DÖSİMM schedules) and gives a date-split budgeting method, a worked route total, the MuseumPass Türkiye vs İstanbul distinction and an on-the-day tariff check, separating confirmed figures from open points.

quality.reviewNotes: Independent review 2026-10-27. Opened all 9 sources. 2027 foreign-visitor site prices checked against Turizm Güncel and FTNnews (agree; Anatolian Civilizations conflicts: free vs €13, flagged). 1 April 2027 date and MuseumPass prices/validity (Türkiye €185/15d, İstanbul €120/5d, Aegean €105/7d, Mediterranean €100/7d, Cappadocia €75/3d) and Ephesus+Terrace Houses €57/72h checked against alomaliye.com reposts of DÖSİMM schedules III and II (letter E-21871808-166.06.99-8860139) and FTNnews; presented as reported/announced with an instruction to confirm on muze.gov.tr. Current prices (Ephesus 40, Pamukkale 30, Galata 30, Göreme 20, Zelve 12, Kaymaklı/Derinkuyu 13, Istanbul Archaeology 15, Bodrum Underwater 20, Anatolian Civilizations 12, Mevlana free) match the tariff table in the muze.gov.tr directive PDF and are labelled as the currently published table; TL collection at previous-day CBRT rate (Art. 6(4)), night-museum separate pricing/no exemptions (Art. 4(ç), 8(4)) from the directive; Experience Museum inclusion from the muze.gov.tr Ephesus page; Göreme night programme to 1 Nov from muze.gov.tr homepage. Worked totals (€160/€181/€115/€193) recomputed. Hedged: ministry original not on ministry sites, pre-purchase price lock, per-site pass coverage, discount eligibility. Independent reviewer fixes applied 2026-10-27: hedged excerpt/intro attribution, explicit muze.gov.tr confirmation, added current Derinkuyu/Bodrum/Anatolian Civilizations prices, corrected discount wording (no residence-card rule in directive), removed ES gate-word false positives.
